title: Why Your Social Media Strategy is Failing (The 9-Video Rule) | Saad Khaja @saadsells
one_sentence_summary: Saad Khaja reveals his content and sales strategies, emphasizing that scalable social growth comes from raw authenticity, singular hyper-niche positioning, and evaluating content concepts within a strict 9-video trial window.
key_takeaways: Apply the 9-Video Rule: Evaluate any new content concept across 9 videos; if it fails to gain traction within this window, pivot immediately instead of wasting months on a dead idea.
Embrace Polarizing Authenticity: Trying to make universally likable, safe content results in low engagement, whereas authentic, polarizing content creates active discussion and virality.
Stick to a Singular Hyper-Niche per Account: Successful social media pages are built on a single, consistent concept rather than mixing multiple unrelated topics on one profile.
Prioritize Raw Cuts Over Flashy Edits: Overly animated and graphic-heavy 'Hormozi-style' captions have become saturated; simple jump-cuts that eliminate filler words perform better.
Treat Cold Calling as Curiosity, Not Pitching: Cold calls fail when salespeople pitch immediately; successful callers use pattern interrupts and ask genuine questions to uncover prospect needs.
Demonstrate Value Above Price: Sales conversions occur when you clearly show the prospect that the value behind the wall far exceeds the cost of breaking it.

actionable_frameworks.name: The 9-Video Rule
actionable_frameworks.description: A rapid testing framework where a new content format is published over 9 consecutive posts to determine viability; if metrics do not lift within 9 posts, the concept is abandoned.

actionable_frameworks.name: Content Value Triad
actionable_frameworks.description: A content classification model based on Value, Entertainment, and Emotion, where single-pillar content reaches tens of thousands of views, two-pillar content reaches hundreds of thousands, and combining all three hits millions.

actionable_frameworks.name: ACA Framework (Acknowledge, Complement, Ask)
actionable_frameworks.description: An objection-handling methodology for sales where you acknowledge the prospect's concern, complement their situation, and ask a clarifying question to reframe their perspective.

actionable_frameworks.name: Old Friend Opener
actionable_frameworks.description: A cold-call pattern interrupt technique where you greet the prospect casually by first name (e.g., 'Peter, how's your day going?') to lower their guard by making them question if they already know you.

actionable_frameworks.name: Killing the Baby
actionable_frameworks.description: An editing mental model requiring creators to delete even their favorite scene in a video if it only satisfies personal vanity without serving value, entertainment, or emotion.

memorable_quotes: If you are not finding hate comments on your page, there is something wrong with your content.
Great sales people understand it's only about asking questions.
Cut your losses. Don't be arrogant; accept defeat and try another concept.
